spec.name: Dutch Windmill
spec.description: A chunky, cheerful Animal Crossing-style Dutch tower windmill with a red-brick octagonal tower, a teal cap roof, a wraparound gallery, a tail pole and four cream-cloth lattice sails.
spec.layout:
Toy-like and chunky. Sides are 8-sided (octagonal), edges are beveled, and nothing is thinner than about 0.05 m. Palette is warm and pastel. Everything is centred on x=0 and the front is +Z.

From the bottom up: a stone plinth (r 2.1, y 0-0.5), then a tapering octagonal brick tower (r 1.9 at y 0.4 to r 1.3 at y 5.0). The lower tower is brick red. Above the gallery the tower turns cream plaster, with a wavy brick/plaster boundary at about y 3.1. A wooden gallery deck (r 2.6, y 1.0-1.2) rings the tower with a railing (top y 1.9). Three wooden steps lead down the front, from z 2.6 to z 3.2. The arched green door is on the front of the tower at deck level, y 1.2-2.5. Small round-topped windows with white frames and flower boxes sit at y 2.9 and y 4.1 on four faces.

On top is a teal cap roof. It is a short drum (r 1.5, y 5.0-5.5) with a dome above it up to y 6.9, plus a finial/weather vane to 7.4. The cap's front is slightly bulged and has a shaft opening. A long sloping wooden tail pole runs from the back of the cap (y 5.2, z -1.4) down to a small post and wheel at y 0.45, z -3.3, with a ladder rail and a rope loop.

The sail shaft exits the cap at [0, 5.7, 1.2]. A round hub/spinner cap (r 0.3) sits at z 1.75. Four sail arms (stocks) of length 3.8 m radiate from the hub, rotated to a rest pose of 45 degrees (an X shape, never straight up/down). Each arm carries a cream cloth lattice panel (0.9 wide, 2.8 long, starting 0.9 from the hub on the trailing edge) framed in wood with cross-bars and a golden trim strip. The sail plane is at z 1.95.

Small props (flour sacks, barrel, lantern, flower pots and tufts at the base) sit on the gallery and around the plinth. The whole model is made of flat-colour primitives. Style cues: puffy proportions, soft rounded tops on windows and door, warm light-coloured trim details, and small flowers and leaf tufts in clusters.

parts.builds: Stone plinth and wooden gallery. Octagonal lathe plinth (r 2.1 at bottom, r 1.95 at top, y 0-0.5, stone with a darker stoneDark skirt ring and a few stoneDark cobble blocks). Round gallery deck (r 2.6, y 1.0-1.2, woodWarm planks with woodDark plank seams as thin parts). Below the deck, eight corbel brackets/posts in woodDark going down into the tower wall, plus a ring beam. A railing around the deck: posts every 22.5 degrees (woodLight, 0.7 m tall, rounded caps), a top rail and a mid rail as swept loops (woodWarm), with the rail opened at the front for the stairs (width 1.2 around z+). Three chunky steps down the front, from stairTop to stairBottom: tops at y 0.8, 0.4 and 0.0 (woodLight with woodDark risers), with small side rails. A doormat strip in trim colour at the top step. Does NOT include the tower wall, door, props or plants.
parts.attaches: Plinth top meets the tower at towerBase / plinthTop (r 1.9). The deck ring sits on galleryDeck and its inner edge tucks into the tower wall. Steps end at stairBottom on y=0. The props part sits on the deck.

parts.builds: The tapering octagonal tower, r 1.9 at y 0.4 to r 1.3 at y 5.0 (use a lathe with 8 segments, or a loft with {ngon:8} sections). Lower tower up to y ~3.1 is brickRed. Add brick details as small parts: horizontal brickDark mortar bands every 0.35 m, scattered brickLight and brickDark brick blocks seated on the faces, and a stone-coloured base skirt at the bottom. The upper tower, from a wavy boundary at about y 3.1 to y 5.0, is plaster, with plasterShade corner quoins/vertical ribs on the 8 edges and a plasterShade ring band at the top (y 4.85-5.0). A woodDark ring beam at y 3.1 hides the colour boundary. Front door at doorFront: an arch-topped door (door colour) 0.9 wide x 1.3 tall, with a woodDark frame, a stone step, a woodLight plank seam, a trim-coloured round handle, and a small round window above the door in glow. Windows: round-topped windows, glass colour with white-plaster frames and cross mullions, 4 at y 2.9 (on +Z, -Z, +X, -X faces, so the front window faces are offset from the door) and 4 at y 4.1. Small woodWarm shutters on both sides of each. Each window has a tiny window box (woodWarm) with leaf tufts and flowerPink/flowerYellow dots. Also a small trim-coloured plaque with the year/emblem above the door, as a flat disc with a darker cross. All details sit on the tower surface (use surface hits or compute radius at height).
parts.attaches: Bottom is sunk into the plinth at towerBase. The gallery deck wraps around it at y 1.0-1.2. The cap sits on the towerTop (r 1.3, y 5.0). The door stands on galleryDeck at the front.

parts.builds: The turning cap roof, riding joint 'cap'. A drum at capBase: octagonal, r 1.5, y 5.0-5.5, in roofDark, with a roofLight rim ring at the bottom. Above it a dome (lathe, 8-12 segments, roof colour) from r 1.5 at y 5.5 to a top at y 6.9, with roofLight shingle rows (thin tapered stripes or overlapping scale bands) and roofDark seam ribs running up the dome. The front of the cap bulges forward with a rounded woodDark bay around the shaft opening at shaftExit (a ring r 0.45, iron inside as a dark hole, plus a woodWarm bearing collar). A small round dormer window with a glow glass and a roofLight hood sits at the back-left and back-right. At the top of the dome is a woodDark post, a trim-coloured ball and a little weathervane (an iron arrow with a leaf-shaped tail in trim). Tail pole: a long woodWarm beam (r 0.09-0.12) from tailPoleRoot (y 5.2, z -1.4) sloping down to tailPoleEnd (y 0.45, z -3.3), with woodDark cross braces, a ladder-like rail of 5 rungs, an iron ring or rope loop of rope-coloured (use sack) swept loop, and at the bottom a woodLight post with a small woodDark wheel (cylinder r 0.25) and a stone anchor block. All of this is on joint 'cap'. Nothing on the cap hangs in front of the sail plane (z > 1.7).
parts.attaches: Sits on top of the tower at capBase / towerTop (r 1.3, y 5.0), with its drum slightly overhanging the tower. The shaft opening is at shaftExit, where the sails part's shaft starts. The tail pole is rooted on the cap's back at tailPoleRoot and ends near the floor at tailPoleEnd.

parts.builds: The sail assembly, riding joint 'sailShaft' (bone along +Z). A woodDark shaft (r 0.14) from shaftExit to the hub (z 1.2-1.8). A hub: woodWarm drum r 0.38 (z 1.65-1.95) with a trim ring, an iron bolt-ring, and a rounded roofLight spinner nose cone (r 0.3, tip to z 2.3). Four arms at rest rotation of 45, 135, 225 and 315 degrees about the z axis (an X shape; never straight up/down). Each arm is built in local coordinates: a woodWarm stock 0.14 thick x 3.8 long from the hub (radial distance 0.3 to 3.8) at plane z 1.95, with a rounded woodDark tip cap. Next to it, on the trailing side, is a lattice sail panel from 0.9 to 3.7 of radial length, 0.95 wide: a woodLight outer frame (0.06 bars), 4-5 woodDark cross-bars, plus a cream 'cloth' (cloth colour) filling 2-3 panes in a checker/triangular arrangement. Each frame has a trim-coloured strip along the outer edge and a small trim triangle/pennant at the tip. Add small iron brackets where each stock meets the hub. The sail plane sits between z 1.9 and 2.05 (lattice slightly in front of the stock, at z 2.0). Sail tips reach about 2.7 m from the hub in both x and y at 45 degrees (x within +-2.75, y 3.0-8.4). Keep all sail geometry within z 1.0-2.4.
parts.attaches: The shaft begins inside the cap at shaftExit and the hub centres on hub (0, 5.7, 1.75). Nothing touches the tower or gallery. The cap's front bay surrounds the shaft.

parts.builds: The cosy details on the gallery and around the base, all small and chunky and riding 'mill'. On the deck at the back-right and left: a stack of three flour sacks (sack colour, rounded boxes, with a woodDark tie and a trim stripe), a woodWarm barrel with woodDark hoops (iron hoops) and a woodLight lid, and a small woodWarm crate. A hanging lantern on an iron bracket by the door at doorFront +0.8 x (iron cage, glow centre, trim cap). Around the plinth: three flower beds as low stoneDark-edged lumps on the ground next to the plinth (not the stairs): each a leaf/leafDark mound with 6-10 tiny flowerPink and flowerYellow bud spheres and little petals, plus bushes (squashed leaf/leafDark spheres clustered) at 45 degrees and 225 degrees around the plinth, radius 2.3-2.6 from the centre. Two terracotta-coloured (brickLight) flower pots on the top step flanking the door, with leaf tufts and flowers. A little woodWarm sign post (signboard in woodLight with a trim-coloured wheat/sail emblem) at the left of the stairs at x 0.9-1.3 (use +X), z ~3.0. All pieces are sized to the gallery and plinth; avoid blocking the door (x -0.6..0.6 at z>1.85) and the stair centre.
parts.attaches: Props stand on y=0 around the plinth (floor) and on galleryDeck (y 1.2) around the gallery edge, outside the door zone. The lantern bracket is fixed to the tower wall beside the door.

calls.reasoning:
I'm settling on a rigged design for the Dutch windmill: a root "mill" spine at the origin, with "base" and a rotating "cap" beneath it. The sails will hang off the cap as a hinge joint rotating around the z-axis, while the hub stays a simple unjointed prop.

I'm sizing the mill now: a tapered tower about 5 m tall, a cap at around y 5, and a shaft at y 5.7 with the hub sitting out toward +Z. I'm shortening the sails to about 3.8 m so their lower tips clear the gallery railing.

I'm checking the sail geometry against the gallery: at 45° the lowest tip drops to about y 3.0, and the overall height comes out near 8.5 with the finial at 7.3.

I'm checking the overall footprint now: the gallery width works out to about 5.4 m, and the total size should come to roughly 5.4 by 8.5 by 6.0. I'm also weighing a tail pole at the back and where the front edge lands relative to the sails.

I'm placing the base as a stone plinth with a gallery platform and railing around the tower, keeping the deck near y 1.2 and the tower radius around 1.85 at that height.

I'm sketching the tower as a tapered octagon from about y 0.4 to 5.0, narrowing from radius 1.9 to 1.3. I'm adding a red brick lower section with a cream upper, an arched door facing front at gallery level, windows with flower boxes, and a timber belt, keeping the tower itself off the floor since the plinth already sits there. The cap goes on top as a rotating dome spanning y 5.0 to 7.0.

I'm finishing the cap's details: a shingled dome with a rim, a front wall with the shaft hole, and a weather vane finial. The tail pole runs from the cap's back down toward the floor, so I'll add a small post or wheel at its end to ground it.

I'm laying out the sail box and hub placement against the cap and gallery, checking that the blades won't collide with the railing since they sit at different heights. I'm also considering a fifth group of surrounding props like flower beds, barrels, and a lantern.

I'm allotting budgets to the five parts, base, tower, cap, sails, and props, and setting the joints: the root mill spine, the cap hinged upward at y 5.0, and the sail shaft hinged along z from the cap.

I'm now picking the color palette: warm pastel brick reds, creams, and stone greys for the masonry, warm wood tones, and teal roof shades to match the cozy look.

I'm listing out the color palette now, with brick reds, creams, and stone greys, plus warm wood tones and teal roof shades, and I'm trying to keep the total under 24 colors.

I'm trimming the palette down to 24 colors by dropping the extra entries, and I'm mapping out the mounts next, starting with the plinth top and the gallery deck at radius 2.6.

I'm working out the mill's overall bounds, so the tower top and hub mounts land at the right heights, and I'm lengthening the footprint to 6.6 so the front stairs fit between the gallery and the ground.

I'm placing the stairs at the front, three steps stepping up from the ground to the deck, and then I'm capping the tower top at y 5.0 with a cap rim around radius 1.5. The cap dome will rise to about 7.0 with the finial reaching 7.4, shaped as a lathed dome with a slight front overhang, and the rim spans y 5.0 to 5.5.

I'm noting the shaft at 5.7 and checking the sails: at 45° the lowest tip clears the gallery at about y 3.0. I'm planning the write-up with builder orientation notes, with blades rotated 45° about z, 3.8-long arms, and a lattice about 0.9 wide.

I'm writing out the final layout as JSON now, with the bevel and thin-part rules kept in mind.

I'm sketching out the tower geometry, deciding between a lathe with 8 segments or building the shape with plain geometry. The radius tapers linearly with height, and I'm working out how an octagonal profile should place its vertices.
